summary: Dune: Imperium blends worker placement with deck building, so each turn you play cards from a small hand to gain agents you send to board spaces, all while racing rivals for limited spots and building military strength for a combat phase at round's end. The tension between deck-building efficiency, faction politics, and open-drafting for combat cards creates a tight, multi-path race to whichever victory condition you can reach first.
praised: Elegant fusion of deck-building with worker placement, each feeding the other
Strong theme integration via factions, Spice, and combat
Multiple viable paths to victory (military, political, economic)
Tense space-blocking since only one player can occupy most spots
criticised: Can feel swingy or 'take that' when combat losses gut a player's board position
Early turns give little agency until deck develops
Some randomness in card draw can undercut careful planning
Rich-get-richer dynamics if one player pulls ahead on Spice or troops

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial, plus open conflict via combat

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Victory points come mainly from a few big swings: controlling Arrakeen/high council spots, winning combat, and completing faction alliances, rather than accumulating many small point sources
